描述_ZN: Scroll of "The Magpie in the Willow", modern, painted by Xu Beihong, on paper with color, 100 cm long and 61.5 cm wide.　　Self-titled: "In the spring of 1933, Beihong wrote this in congratulation of the completion of the new residence of Huaju Rendi at Lihang Middle School." Inscribed with a seal in vermilion underneath: "Sorrow". One seal of the collection is indistinct and illegible.　　Thirty-three years that refers to the Republic of 33 years (1944), Xu Beihong was 49 years old.　　In 1944, Xu Beihong suffered from hypertension and nephritis in Chongqing hospital for six months, the medical advice not to move the brush to do painting. As a result, the number of his creations dropped sharply that year. The present painting was painted by him at the beginning of the year at the invitation of a friend, and is very rare. Six magpies are perched on the branches of a willow tree, two of which are clinging to each other, whispering and attracting the other magpies to stop and watch.　　The picture is cleverly conceived, with the magpies either single or double, forming a "c" shape, with sparse or dense distances and high or low positions between them, making the picture rich in rhythmic changes and vividness. The painting is full of willow branches fluttering in the wind, which are outlined with a medium sharp brush, and the lines are thick and thin and elastic, showing the author's solid line drawing skills. The willow branches are linked together with the scattered magpies, and together they compose a joyful spring song to wish Hua Ju Rendi a happy completion of his new residence.
